**Park Ji‑sung** (박지성) is a retired South Korean professional footballer who played primarily as a midfielder. He was born on **June 12, 1981** in Seoul, South Korea.

### Career Highlights

| Period | Club | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| 1999–2000 | Suwon Samsung Bluewings (K League) | Started his professional career in South Korea. |
| 2000–2005 | PSV Eindhoven (Netherlands) | Became a key player in the Eredivisie, winning the league in 2004–05. |
| 2005–2012 | Manchester United (England) | Joined the Premier League club for a record fee for a Korean player at the time. Won three Premier League titles, the FA Cup, the League Cup, the UEFA Champions League (2008–09), and the FIFA Club World Cup. Known for his work‑rate, stamina, and versatility. |
| 2012–2013 | Inter Milan (Italy) | Brief stint in Serie A. |
| 2013–2014 | FC Seoul (K League) | Returned to South Korea to finish his playing career. |

### International Career

- Represented the **South Korea national team** from 2000 to 2014.
- Earned **108 caps** and scored **12 goals**.
- Key player in South Korea’s 2002 FIFA World Cup run to the quarter‑finals, where they famously defeated Italy.
- Participated in multiple AFC Asian Cups and Olympic tournaments.

### Style of Play

- Renowned for his exceptional stamina and ability to cover large areas of the pitch.
- Versatile midfielder capable of playing both defensive and attacking roles.
- Known for his powerful long‑range shots and precise passing.

### Post‑Retirement

- After retiring from professional football, Park Ji‑sung has been involved in various media appearances, coaching roles, and ambassadorial duties.
- He has also worked as a football analyst and commentator for Korean sports networks.

### Personal Life

- Married to **Kim Hye‑jin**, a former Miss Korea, in 2014.
- They have two children together.

Park Ji‑sung is widely regarded as one of the most influential Korean footballers of his generation and remains a respected figure in both Korean and international football circles.
